summary: Koshko et al. report a sex-specific exposure effect from individual offspring libraries. HypoExplorer sums the same retained P21 male libraries within three litters per arm before fitting the exposure effect. The labelled gene-expression panel, supplements and public deposits did not supply author effects for those litter aggregates.

manualReview.summary: Published P21 male offspring results use a different replicate unit from the registered litter-level contrast.
manualReview.note: After Xist-based sex reassignment and exclusion of OBFH14, GEO identifies 9 filtered-air and 6 benzene-exposed male offspring libraries. The authors describe DESeq2/apeglm analysis separately by sex after a total-count filter of 20, with BH-adjusted P < 0.1. The paper gives no design formula or litter-aggregation step. Figure 1B displays selected gene-expression averages by sex and exposure. The registered male edgeR quasi-likelihood fit compares within-litter sums from three litters per arm. The publisher and preprint supplements show glial imaging and body composition, and all 33 GEO sample supplements contain only STAR counts. No gene-level author table or figure panel for the registered analysis was located.
reviewFlags: Sibling libraries contribute to the published offspring analysis. The independent observations in the registered fit are litters. Gene-level litter effects and their P/FDR remain unassessed.

verificationReview.reason: The available author gene directions describe benzene versus filtered air within male offspring at P21. HypoExplorer fits an exposure coefficient to three litter aggregates per arm. Figure 1B averages expression by sex and treatment, and no public source reviewed reports a gene-level effect for the six-litter analysis.
verificationReview.nextStep: Reopen if author gene-level benzene-versus-filtered-air effects become available for the same post-exclusion P21 male libraries summed within each of the six litters. Check the sample mapping, direction, identifiers and reported scope before comparison.
